headline: Oak launches with $60M funding to fix AI agent identity mess
summary: Israeli startup Oak emerges from stealth with $60 million in seed funding, offering an AI-native identity management solution for enterprises. Its platform aims to secure access for humans and AI agents in complex digital environments.
details: Israeli startup Oak has officially emerged from stealth, announcing its product is generally available and already deployed by enterprise clients. The company secured $60 million in seed funding late last year to address the growing complexities of identity management in an era of AI agents.

Traditional identity management tools, even those built for the cloud, are proving inadequate as humans and AI agents increasingly work together in digital environments. Outdated credentials and poor Identity Access Management (IAM) are common security vulnerabilities that AI is expected to exacerbate.

Oak positions itself as an AI-native replacement for legacy tools, offering a unified control plane for identity across an organization. Its AI connector framework maps access to actual app usage, enabling real-time removal of unneeded permissions rather than relying on manual periodic reviews.

Co-founded by serial entrepreneur Shai Morag and chief product officer Tal Marom, Oak developed its product after extensive consultations with 100 CISOs and IAM leaders. Morag's background includes selling cyber startup Secdo to Palo Alto Networks and serving as CPO at Ermetic.

The substantial $60 million seed round was co-led by Accel, CRV, and Greylock Partners, with additional participation from AlphaDrive Ventures, Hetz Ventures, and angel investors. Investors cited Morag's strong track record in cybersecurity as a key factor in their decision.

Oak plans to invest heavily in R&D and growth, aiming to scale rapidly to compete in a complex market where vendor lock-in is deep. The company is actively hiring, particularly in the U.S., where the majority of its staff will soon be based.

headline_marked: [[NotebookLM converts unread articles into video]] with customizable visual styles like Anime
headline: NotebookLM converts unread articles into video with customizable visual styles like Anime
summary: NotebookLM's Studio tab transforms saved articles and documents into narrated videos, offering visual styles from Whiteboard to Anime, making information consumption more engaging.
details: NotebookLM's new Studio tab can convert your existing notebooks into video overviews. This feature helps users process large backlogs of saved articles and documents by transforming them into a more digestible visual format.

Unlike audio-only overviews, video allows for the display of data visualizations and charts, which can convey complex information more effectively. Research suggests the "picture superiority effect" aids retention, making visual learning more impactful.

The platform supports various source types, including PDFs, Google Docs, Slides, Sheets, EPUBs, audio, and URLs, with generous limits of up to 500,000 words or 200MB per source. Google Docs, Sheets, and Slides also sync automatically.

Users can customize the video output with various visual styles like Whiteboard, Retro Print, Watercolor, Paper-craft, Heritage, Kawaii, Classic, and Anime. A custom prompt box allows users to guide the AI on specific points of interest or disagreements between sources.

While useful, the AI can struggle to render complex math formulas and detailed diagrams, and may "fatten" arguments between conflicting sources into a middle ground. Users should double-check content, especially for workplace use.

Visual styles like Anime and Whiteboard are free, with Google charging for volume and advanced formats. "Cinematic" offers an animated film style, while "Short" creates 60-second vertical clips, both available in Pro tiers.
Cinematic and Short formats currently support English output only and are limited to users 18 and over. All processing occurs in the cloud, with video generation times sometimes exceeding 30 minutes.
